title: ExxonMobil (NYSE:XOM) Shares Up 1.8% - What's Next? - MarketBeat
content:
Shares of ExxonMobil Corporation (NYSE:XOM - Get Free Report) shot up 1.8% on Monday. The company traded as high as $172.55 and last traded at $172.0170. 8,762,062 shares were traded during trading, a decline of 52% from the average daily volume of 18,074,795 shares. The stock had previously closed at $168.94. XOM has been the topic of several recent analyst reports. Barclays cut their price objective on shares of ExxonMobil from $182.00 to $177.00 and set an "overweight" rating on the stock in a report on Monday, August 17th. Wells Fargo & Company reaffirmed an "equal weight" rating and issued a $182.00 price target on shares of ExxonMobil in a report on Thursday, October 1st. DZ Bank downgraded ExxonMobil from a "buy" rating to a "hold" rating and set a $156.00 price target on the stock. in a research note on Tuesday, August 4th. Mizuho cut their price objective on ExxonMobil from $175.00 to $170.00 and set a "neutral" rating on the stock in a report on Thursday, July 9th. Finally, Weiss Ratings upgraded ExxonMobil from a "buy (b-)" rating to a "buy (b)" rating in a research note on Tuesday, September 29th. Eleven research analysts have rated the stock with a Buy rating and fourteen have issued a Hold rating to the stock. According to MarketBeat, the stock has an average rating of "Hold" and a consensus target price of $164.78. The stock has a market cap of $713.00 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 22.14, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 0.99 and a beta of 0.21. The stock's 50 day moving average price is $161.67 and its two-hundred day moving average price is $154.18. The company has a quick ratio of 0.85, a current ratio of 1.13 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.12. ExxonMobil (NYSE:XOM - Get Free Report) last posted its earnings results on Friday, July 31st. The oil and gas company reported $3.52 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, missing analysts' consensus estimates of $3.56 by ($0.04). ExxonMobil had a net margin of 8.88% and a return on equity of 13.14%. The business had revenue of $114.53 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $109.94 billion. During the same quarter in the prior year, the firm earned $1.64 earnings per share.  Equities research analysts forecast that ExxonMobil Corporation will post 12.40 EPS for the current fiscal year. The business also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, September 10th. Stockholders of record on Monday, August 17th were issued a $1.03 dividend. This represents a $4.12 annualized dividend and a dividend yield of 2.4%. The ex-dividend date of this dividend was Monday, August 17th. ExxonMobil's payout ratio is 53.02%. A number of hedge funds have recently modified their holdings of the stock. jvl associates llc raised its holdings in shares of ExxonMobil by 2.6% in the 3rd quarter. jvl associates llc now owns 2,862 shares of the oil and gas company's stock valued at $466,000 after purchasing an additional 73 shares in the last quarter.  Market Street Wealth Management Advisors LLC lifted its position in shares of ExxonMobil by 42.6% during the 3rd quarter. Market Street Wealth Management Advisors LLC now owns 2,621 shares of the oil and gas company's stock worth $427,000 after purchasing an additional 783 shares during the last quarter.  Baring Financial LLC lifted its position in shares of ExxonMobil by 8.4% during the 3rd quarter. Baring Financial LLC now owns 6,220 shares of the oil and gas company's stock worth $1,012,000 after purchasing an additional 484 shares during the last quarter.  Colton Groome Financial Advisors LLC grew its stake in shares of ExxonMobil by 2.5% during the third quarter. Colton Groome Financial Advisors LLC now owns 3,668 shares of the oil and gas company's stock worth $597,000 after purchasing an additional 91 shares in the last quarter.  Finally, Byrne Asset Management LLC grew its stake in shares of ExxonMobil by 11.5% during the third quarter. Byrne Asset Management LLC now owns 9,752 shares of the oil and gas company's stock worth $1,598,000 after purchasing an additional 1,002 shares in the last quarter. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 61.80% of the company's stock. Exxon Mobil Corporation, commonly known as ExxonMobil, is an integrated energy company engaged in the exploration, development, production and sale of crude oil and natural gas. The company also manufactures and markets fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals and specialty products used in transportation, industrial and consumer applications. ExxonMobil operates across the energy value chain through businesses that include upstream oil and natural gas production, refining and fuels marketing, chemical manufacturing, and lower-carbon solutions. title: CVX Outpaces Industry in Past 6 Months: Should Investors Stay Bullish? - The Globe and Mail
content: Over the past six months, shares of Chevron CorporationCVX have outpaced both its sub-industry and the broader energy sector. The stock gained 10.6%, outperforming the sub-industry and the energy sector’s rise of 7.2% and 7.4%, respectively. Despite concerns surrounding oil demand, crude price fluctuations and evolving geopolitical conditions, Chevron continues to distinguish itself as a leading integrated energy company. Its strong track record of shareholder returns, high-quality asset base, solid balance sheet, operational strength and favorable earnings outlook support its potential for sustainable growth. At the same time, volatility in global energy markets and elevated oil prices could create an attractive opportunity to invest in a high-quality producer with low-cost operations and resilient cash generation. For investors looking for a blend of stability, income and long-term growth potential, Chevron’s current position may offer an appealing entry point. With energy demand and production expected to remain important over the long term, here’s why CVX remains a compelling stock to consider for investors seeking energy exposure in 2026. Chevron's cash-generation outlook and financial discipline provide a strong foundation for shareholder returns. Management expects adjusted free cash flow to grow by more than 10% annually on average through 2030 at its stated commodity assumptions while targeting a dividend-plus-capex breakeven below $50 Brent. Its $1.78 quarterly dividend per share and continuing buybacks reflect a commitment to capital returns. The 20-year Microsoft power agreement for 2.67 gigawatts adds an opportunity for contracted, oil-price-independent cash flows, subject to successful project execution. The company's dividend yield of 3.36% is particularly attractive, demonstrating strength against peers like Shell plc SHEL and Exxon Mobil Corporation XOM, which offer a lower yield comparatively. Chevron's upstream portfolio offers a clear path to higher production, supported by Guyana, the Permian Basin and the Gulf of America. The Hess acquisition adds long-life, high-margin Guyana barrels, while management targets 2%-3% annual production growth through 2030. Chevron's September agreement in Venezuela provides further upside through new Orinoco Belt acreage and improved commercial terms. Its joint ventures plan to invest more than $7 billion over five years and more than double production to about 600,000 barrels a day from 2026 levels, with total costs below $20 per barrel. These developments could extend Chevron's resource base, broaden its growth opportunities and support cash generation beyond this decade. ExxonMobil also stands to benefit from its Guyana and the Permian Basin assets as they support higher production and improved unit profitability, and Shell recently completed the acquisition of ARC Resources, which will expand its Integrated Gas business and increase production growth through 2030. Chevron's focus on lowering operating costs should strengthen profitability even without a sustained rise in oil prices. The company achieved $3 billion in annualized structural savings and $1.5 billion in Hess-related synergies ahead of schedule. Its recent agreement to transfer Hess Midstream interests and DJ Basin crude midstream assets is expected to cut Bakken unit midstream costs by about 50% and lift return on capital employed by 0.5%. The deal should also remove roughly $3.7 billion of Hess Midstream debt from Chevron's consolidated balance sheet upon closing. At the same time, ExxonMobil's $16.3 billion in cost savings since 2019 supports its $20 billion target by 2030, with operational efficiencies expected to keep cash costs broadly flat. Shell's $700 million savings in 2026 support its $5-$7 billion cost reduction target, with AI and operational efficiencies set to boost free cash flow. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CVX’s 2026 earnings is pegged at $17.34 per share, indicating 137.9% year-over-year growth. To own ExxonMobil Holdings, you need to believe the integrated model, from Permian and Guyana barrels to refining and chemicals, can keep turning a volatile commodity stream into steady cash generation. The recent crude price spike from the Gulf disruptions mostly reinforces that story in the near term, but the key short term catalyst remains execution on high return upstream projects and cost savings. The biggest operational risk right now is that oil and gas demand or regulations tighten faster than the project slate and early low carbon bets can adapt, which could pressure margins. The latest supply shock moves the needle on quarterly earnings sensitivity, but it does not materially change that broader risk reward equation. Among recent developments, the progress in Guyana is most relevant. Guyana has already recovered about US$55b of investment and operating costs almost two years ahead of schedule, and upstream volumes outside the Middle East are at a multi decade high. For a shareholder watching this crude spike, the question is how efficiently ExxonMobil can keep bringing those lower cost barrels into the system. That early payback, together with structural savings of US$16.3b since 2019 and a target of at least US$20b by 2030, frames the catalyst investors are really tracking. Supply shocks may swing quarterly results, but the medium term story depends on whether ExxonMobil can keep costs flat, stick to disciplined capex and convert Guyana and Permian output into durable free cash flow despite commodity volatility. ExxonMobil Holdings' current analyst narrative points to revenues of US$373.7b and earnings of US$45.7b by 2029. That profile assumes 1.2% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$12.9b from US$32.8b today. Some of the most optimistic ExxonMobil analysts lean hard into regulatory relief as a swing factor. Before this Gulf supply shock, the bullish cohort was already penciling in US$508.7b of revenue and US$55.2b of earnings by 2029. You can see how a fresh, supply-driven price spike could push those optimistic views even further or prompt a rethink, so it is worth exploring a range of expectations rather than anchoring on one forecast set.
